question.text: What is the Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG) tax rate on equity mutual fund units held for more than 12 months (FY 2025-26)?

explanation.text: The Logic: For equity-oriented mutual fund units held for more than 12 months, gains are treated as Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG). Following the Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024 (effective for transfers on or after 23 July 2024), LTCG on listed equity / equity-oriented schemes is taxed at a flat 12.5%, with the first Rs. 1.25 lakh of such LTCG in a financial year exempt. This applies to equity funds and equity-oriented hybrid funds (typically 65%+ equity). The Trap: "10% above Rs. 1 lakh" is the older LTCG regime, since revised. "15% above Rs. 1.25 lakh" mixes the new exemption with the old STCG rate. "20% with indexation benefit" is a pre-2023 debt-fund concept; equity LTCG never benefited from indexation. Note: The cited NISM Series V-B workbook pages (119-121) support the 12-month holding period and the Rs. 1.25 lakh LTCG exemption, but do not explicitly state the 12.5% LTCG rate. The framing above reflects current Income Tax Act provisions as revised by Finance (No. 2) Act, 2024.
